motive.message:
Add a required reason argument to issue_refund, stored with the refund
record and documented in the tool schema and README. Cap each run at
3 model calls and 150 max_tokens per call.
motive.note: The commit names Entire checkpoint d098c3973305, and Entire cannot find it, so the request behind this commit is not on record.

brief.headline: c54575368397 cut max_steps to 3, leaving no budget to recover from truncated batch tool calls

sentences.text: Commit c54575368397 reduced max_steps from 8 to 3 and max_tokens from 300 to 150, meaning the agent has no spare model calls to recover when a batched tool call is truncated.

In the failing run, the 150-token cap causes the third LLM response at acbf23c5 to be cut off mid-JSON, so the second issue_refund call arrives with only order_id and no amount or reason, producing the error at 6e23affa.
Similarly, the first LLM call at 0abc1926 was truncated so that the second lookup_order call arrived with no arguments, causing the error at 4d831c6b and forcing an extra recovery call.
That recovery call consumed the third and final model slot at 0da4439e just to re-look up order 6006, leaving no calls left after 6e23affa to retry the failed refund.

In the passing run at b467d5b0fed2, max_steps was 8 and max_tokens was 300, so both lookup_order calls fit in one response at 1e654c3a and both issue_refund calls fit in one response at 8172ddce with no errors.

Because truncation depends on how the model serialises multiple tool calls into one response, failures are intermittent—matching the ~14% failure rate observed from c54575368397 onward across checkpoint d098c3973305.
